key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant: even though many point defects introduce deep gap levels, they contribute too little Shockley-Read-Hall recombination to explain the observed photovoltaic efficiency losses.
engineering_relevance: This suggests t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, where defect robustness can simplify materials optimization and device design.
method: First-principles calculations of point defects in trigonal selenium
Computed defect-assisted SRH recombination via nonradiative multi-phonon emission and radiative capture
Surveyed a large, chemically diverse defect set across charge states and doping conditions
evidence_signal: Across the defect data set, large lattice reorganizations and energy releases of at least 0.5 E_G per recombination event strongly suppress nonradiative recombination, and radiative defect-assisted capture is also too small to explain device losses.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on theoretical defect modeling, so device performance can still depend on defect concentrations, processing conditions, and unmodeled extended defects or interfaces.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
